description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between “pop frequency (x10^4)” on the x-axis and “Accuracy” on the y-axis, comparing two metrics: “Initial Accuracy” (green line with square markers and solid line style) and “Final Accuracy” (blue line with triangle markers and dashed line style). The x-axis ranges from approximately 1 to 19 in units of 10^4, with tick marks at intervals of 2 (1, 3, 5, ..., 19). The y-axis is linear, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2. The green “Initial Accuracy” line begins at approximately 0.38 at x=1, rises to a peak of ~0.90 at x=11, then plateaus slightly before ending at ~0.92 at x=17. The blue “Final Accuracy” line starts at ~0.70 at x=1, fluctuates with peaks at x=5 (~1.05) and x=11 (~1.05), dips to ~0.95 at x=9, and ends at ~1.08 at x=17. Error bars are present for both lines, indicating variability, and are generally larger for the blue line, especially at higher x-values. The plot suggests that final accuracy consistently exceeds initial accuracy across all measured frequencies, with both metrics generally increasing as pop frequency increases, though with some fluctuations in the final accuracy trend.
